rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this round escalates obfuscation intensity across all seven passes for this small (1259 text bytes, 12 functions) bit-manipulation benchmark. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain since arithmetic substitution is low-risk and the program's bit-twiddling core (read_x_bits, read_11_bits) benefits strongly from opaque arithmetic; BCF and FLA are pushed high to break control-flow recovery in the hot bit-reading loops, with RuntimeCost weights (0.7/0.5) kept below their security weights so the scheduler still favors applying them but respects the tight five11/main loops. SPLIT is emphasized for DiversityGain because it composes with FLA to fragment the few large basic blocks this tiny program has, at near-zero runtime cost. IBR is raised for block-level indirection between the small functions, while ICALL and IGV get moderate security weights with elevated CorrectnessRisk tags (0.3/0.35) since indirect calls and global variable encoding are the two passes most likely to perturb the pointer-heavy list handling (free_list2) in this benchmark; the risk weights let the feature-driven selector apply them to functions whose features are favorable while sparing risky sites. Overall the table biases every pass toward security/diversity over cost because round 0 confirmed the toolchain handles this program cleanly, and the program's minimal size means SizeCost penalties have little absolute impact.
